newsitem.title: IRAQ: Sirens reported to blare over Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: Sirens reported to blare over Baghdad.

text.p: Air raid sirens blared in parts of the Iraqi capital Baghdad on Tuesday but were not heard all over the city, residents said.
"I heard a siren just for a few seconds but could not determine whether it was a warning, a test or sounding all clear," a resident told Reuters.
The Pentagon said in Washington the United States had launched cruise missile attacks against air defence targets in Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi attacks in the Kurdish north.

U.S. defence officials, who asked not to be identified, said the unmanned and highly-accurate missiles were fired from B-52 bombers and American warships in the Gulf at military targets in and around Baghdad.
There was no official confirmation in Baghdad that the U.S. raids had taken place.
State-run radio continued with its normal programmes, and Iraqis on the street said they did not care if an attack were launched.
Official newspapers appearing on Tuesday had no comment on a possible military strike against Iraq.

The United States last sent cruise missiles against Iraq in June 1993 to avenge an alleged plot to kill former U.S. president George Bush during a visit to Kuwait. The attacks then killed six civilians.
